method: Memory fabs in China, Japan and Korea, advanced-packaging and back-end sites in Malaysia, Thailand and the Philippines, state and national semiconductor programmes (Singapore, Texas, New York, Odisha, Uttar Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Thailand) and equipment models for makers with thin model coverage (AMEC, Nova, FormFactor, Kingsemi, Eugene Technology), from government pages, company releases, product pages and industry news located by web search; titles and search-result summaries.

pr.note: Batch 15: details from the title and search-result summary of the 2011 launch release; page not read. Successor to Primo D-RIE.

pr.tech: Optical CD platform combining multi-channel spectral ellipsometry and spectral reflectometry with spectral interferometry (per Nova)

pr.note: Batch 15: from the Nova materials-metrology product overview summary.

pr.tech: Semi- or fully automated probe system; Velox control software; thermal range −60 °C to +300 °C; fully automated version handles up to fifty 200/300 mm wafers in SEMI-standard cassettes; pads down to 30 µm (per FormFactor)

pr.note: Batch 15: from the Kingsemi product page summary; a 300 mm-only model name was not found.

fa.name: YMTC Wuhan Phase III fab

invest.label: About US$3 billion (Phase III venture, per report title)

fa.capacity: 50,000 wafers per month by 2027 and 100,000 at full capacity; about half reportedly allocated to DRAM (per Reuters-cited reports)
fa.technology: 3D NAND; part of capacity reportedly for DRAM
fa.notes: Phase III company set up Sept 2025. April 2026 reports: construction complete, equipment installation under way, more than half of tools from domestic suppliers. Mass-production target reportedly moved to 2H 2026 from 2027 (a plan). Not confirmed against a YMTC statement in reviewed sources.

fa.name: Kioxia Kitakami Fab2 (K2), Iwate
fa.scheme: Japanese government subsidy (plan approved Feb 2024, per coverage)
fa.capacity: Output ramps in stages; meaningful production expected from 1H 2026 (per release)
fa.technology: 8th-generation 218-layer 3D flash with CBA (CMOS directly Bonded to Array)
fa.notes: Construction was planned to start April 2022 and finish in 2023 (per the 2022 announcement); operation began 29 Sept 2025.

fa.name: SK hynix M15X, Cheongju

invest.label: About 20 trillion won in total (per Apr 2024 report; the fab building alone was put at about 5.3 trillion won)

fa.notes: Opened ahead of schedule with first equipment brought in (Q3 2025 earnings call, 29 Oct 2025); contribution to HBM output planned from 2026. A report that 1b DRAM for HBM4 would start in Feb 2026 is a plan, not a milestone.

fa.name: SK hynix P&T7 advanced packaging fab, Cheongju
fa.notes: Designed to work alongside the M15 fab and M15X (FAC-000046); aimed at raising HBM output by 2027 (per TrendForce title).

fa.name: Intel Penang advanced packaging complex
fa.technology: EMIB and Foveros advanced-packaging assembly and test (phase 1)
fa.notes: Reported 99% complete in 2026, with first-phase operations due later in 2026 (Malaysian PM, per coverage). The project was reported paused in early 2025. No start of operations found in reviewed sources as of Nov 2026.

fa.name: Infineon backend site, Samut Prakan (Thailand)

invest.label: About US$1.4 billion (48 billion baht) for the complex (per Thai coverage / BOI)
More than €100 million initial investment (per TechNews); Evertiq says the amount was not disclosed

fa.capacity: Opened with Module A; designed for up to five modules (per coverage)
fa.technology: Power modules and discretes; wafer test; R&D
fa.jobs: About 350 at opening, rising to about 1,000 as Module A ramps (per coverage)
fa.notes: Opened 1 Oct 2026 with Thailand's Prime Minister attending. Full utilisation of Module A could come in 2027 (a plan). The two investment figures differ in scope and are kept side by side.

fa.name: ATEC production line for PANJIT, Cabuyao (Laguna)
fa.notes: A captive line opened for Taiwan's PANJIT, per the Board of Investments announcement reported by Malaya. A production line within an existing ATEC site, not a new plant.
